name: RiversMAN Mathematics Challenge
description: Annual mathematics competition organised by the Rivers State Mathematical Association (RiversMAN) for secondary school students across Rivers State. Tests algebra, geometry, statistics, and olympiad-level problem-solving across junior and senior divisions.

name: Cowbellpedia Secondary School Mathematics TV Quiz
description: Nigeria's premier mathematics television quiz competition, organised by Promasidor Nigeria Limited. Broadcast nationally on NTA and selected state television stations. Junior and senior categories. One of the most widely watched academic competitions in Nigeria.

name: STEM Olympics Pan-African Championship
description: Pan-African STEM competition bringing together secondary school students from over 20 African nations. Categories include robotics, coding challenge, mathematics relay, physics experiment design, and science communication. Hosted on a rotating country basis.

name: Nigerian Mathematical Olympiad
description: The official national mathematics olympiad that selects Nigeria's team for the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO). Run through a two-stage process: state-level preliminary rounds followed by a national final. Top performers represent Nigeria internationally.

name: Lagos State Inter-School Debate Championship
description: Annual parliamentary debate competition for secondary schools across Lagos State, organised by the Lagos State Ministry of Education. British Parliamentary format. Schools compete in both junior (JSS1–3) and senior (SSS1–3) divisions.

name: Kenya National Science Congress
description: Annual science fair and competition for Kenyan secondary school students organised by the Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) and the Ministry of Education. Projects are evaluated in biology, chemistry, physics, and computer science categories.

name: Ghana National Science & Maths Quiz
description: Ghana's most prestigious secondary school academic competition, broadcast on GTV and Adom TV. Tests science (biology, chemistry, physics) and mathematics in a relay format. Organised by the Ghana Education Service. Nationally followed and highly competitive.

name: East African Schools Debate Championship
description: Annual competitive debate tournament bringing together secondary schools from Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and Rwanda. World Schools Debate format. Host country rotates annually. Aims to build critical thinking and public speaking across East Africa.

name: International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
description: The world's largest pre-college science competition, affiliated to Society for Science. Students win the right to attend by placing first or second at a qualifying affiliated fair. Categories include behavioural science, chemistry, engineering, environmental science, mathematics, and physics.

name: AMC 10/12 (American Mathematics Competition)
description: The AMC 10 and AMC 12 are the first competitions in the series of competitions leading to the USA Mathematical Olympiad (USAMO) and ultimately the IMO. Administered globally. High scorers advance to the AIME, then to USAMO/USAJMO.

name: DECA International Career Development Conference
description: DECA prepares emerging leaders and entrepreneurs in marketing, finance, hospitality and management. The ICDC is the global finals. Competitive events include written exams, role plays, and presentations judged by industry professionals.

name: Science Olympiad National Tournament
description: Science Olympiad is one of the premier science competitions in the US, providing rigorous, standards-based challenges. Each team of 15 members competes in 23 events covering biology, chemistry, physics, earth science, and engineering.

name: The Hague International Model United Nations (THIMUN)
description: One of the world's largest and oldest Model UN conferences, held annually in The Hague, Netherlands. Over 3,200 delegates from across the world. THIMUN is the affiliated body that accredits many school MUN programs globally.

name: Nigerian National Debate Championship
description: The premier national secondary schools debate competition in Nigeria, organised in partnership with the National Association of Debate Coaches (NADC). World Schools Debate format. State winners compete at the national level.

name: Pan-African Mathematics Olympiad (PAMO)
description: Organised under the African Mathematical Union (AMU), PAMO is the African counterpart of the IMO. Countries submit teams of up to six students who compete in a two-day written examination. Results feed into IMO team selections for many African nations.

name: Intercollegiate Athletics Championship (AAA Lagos)
description: Annual inter-school track and field competition for secondary schools across Lagos State, organised by the Amateur Athletic Association of Nigeria (AAAN) Lagos chapter. Disciplines include sprints, relays, long jump, high jump, and field events.

name: Federal Government Science Essay Competition
description: National essay competition for secondary school students in the sciences, organised by the Federal Ministry of Education Nigeria. Students submit essays on STEM topics with national and zonal award stages. Builds science communication skills alongside technical depth.

name: Spelling Bee Nigeria (National Finals)
description: Nigeria's national spelling competition for primary and junior secondary school students. State-level competitions feed into the national finals broadcast on national television. Tests vocabulary breadth, etymology knowledge, and language fluency.

name: National Junior Council MUN Nigeria
description: Model United Nations conference for secondary school students across Nigeria, focused on building diplomatic skills, research capacity, and international affairs awareness. Committees simulate UN bodies including the Security Council, ECOSOC, and UNICEF.

name: Lagos STEM Girls Challenge
description: Annual STEM competition exclusively for female secondary school students in Lagos, aimed at bridging the gender gap in science and technology. Challenges include robotics, coding, and engineering design. Mentored by women in tech working in Lagos.

name: Enact National Business Competition Nigeria
description: Entrepreneurship and business competition for secondary school students across Nigeria. Teams develop business plans addressing real social or economic challenges in their communities. Judged by industry professionals. National finals held annually in Abuja or Lagos.

name: Kenya National Science and Engineering Fair (KNSEF)
description: Kenya's premier science fair for secondary school students, serving as the national qualifying competition for the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF). Projects span biology, chemistry, physics, engineering, mathematics, and computer science. Top finishers represent Kenya internationally.

name: East Africa Science and Engineering Fair
description: Regional science and engineering fair bringing together top student researchers from East African countries. Affiliated with the Intel ISEF network. Projects are evaluated by professional scientists and engineers. Top teams qualify for ISEF.

name: Kenya Secondary Schools Debate Championship
description: National competitive debate championship for Kenyan secondary schools, organised through the Kenya National Debate Federation. World Schools format. County-level winners advance to nationals. Builds critical thinking, public speaking, and argumentation skills.

name: Kenya Mathematics Olympiad
description: National mathematics olympiad for Kenyan secondary school students, selecting Kenya's team for the African Mathematics Olympiad (PAMO) and ultimately the IMO. Run in two rounds: school-level and national final. Organised through the Kenya National Examinations Council.

name: Safaricom Youth Programme Science Competition
description: Science and innovation competition for Kenyan youth supported by the Safaricom Foundation. Focuses on technology solutions for real-world problems in Kenya. Participants develop working prototypes and pitch to judges from Safaricom and industry partners.

name: Ghana Mathematics Olympiad
description: National mathematics competition for Ghanaian secondary school students, organised by the Ghana Education Service. Selects Ghana's team for the Pan-African Mathematics Olympiad (PAMO) and the IMO. Two rounds: district-level and national final.

name: Abii National Quiz Competition (Ghana)
description: One of Ghana's most popular academic quiz competitions for junior and senior secondary school students. Tests science, maths, general knowledge, and current affairs. Broadcast on national television. A stepping stone to the renowned National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ).

name: Ghana Debate Union Championship
description: National debate competition organised by the Ghana Debate Union for secondary school and tertiary students. Uses British Parliamentary and World Schools formats. Annual national championship with regional qualifying rounds across all ten regions of Ghana.

name: South African Mathematics Olympiad (SAMO)
description: South Africa's national mathematics olympiad, organised by the South African Mathematics Foundation (SAMF). Three rounds: junior, intermediate, and senior. Top performers represent South Africa at the IMO and Pan-African Mathematics Olympiad. One of the most prestigious academic competitions on the continent.

name: Eskom Expo for Young Scientists
description: South Africa's largest science fair for learners from Grade 4 to Grade 12, sponsored by Eskom. Regional expos feed into a national competition. The fair covers all scientific disciplines and engineering. Top projects qualify for the Intel ISEF and other international fairs.

name: Old Mutual Science Olympiad (South Africa)
description: Annual science olympiad for South African high school students supported by Old Mutual Foundation. Tests biology, chemistry, and physics. Delivered in three rounds with national finals. Widely used as a university application differentiator.

name: South African Astronomy Olympiad
description: National astronomy competition for South African secondary school students, organised by the South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO). Tests observational astronomy, astrophysics theory, and data analysis. Top performers compete at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA).

name: Ethiopian National Physics Olympiad
description: National physics competition for Ethiopian secondary school students, organised by the Ethiopian Ministry of Education and university physics departments. Selects Ethiopia's team for the International Physics Olympiad (IPhO). Written theory and experimental rounds.

name: AfriCAN Science Olympiad
description: Pan-African science olympiad spanning biology, chemistry, and physics for secondary school students across the African continent. Organised through the African Union's education initiative. Aims to strengthen science education infrastructure across member states.

name: Indian National Mathematical Olympiad (INMO)
description: The second stage of the Mathematical Olympiad Programme in India, following the Regional Mathematical Olympiad (RMO). Administered by the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE). INMO qualifiers form the pool from which India's IMO team is selected.

name: Science Olympiad Foundation Competitions (NSO / IMO / IEO)
description: The Science Olympiad Foundation (SOF) runs a suite of school-level olympiad competitions including the National Science Olympiad (NSO), International Mathematics Olympiad (IMO-SOF), and International English Olympiad (IEO). Recognised by thousands of schools across India and internationally.

name: Young Scientist India Competition
description: National science fair and competition for Indian secondary school students run by the Department of Science and Technology (DST). Students present original research projects. State-level winners advance to national finals. Aligned with the India International Science Festival.

name: International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO)
description: The most prestigious mathematics competition in the world for pre-university students. Held annually in a different country, with national teams of up to 6 students. Problems test creativity and depth in number theory, algebra, combinatorics, and geometry over two days of 4.5-hour exams.

name: International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO)
description: Annual chemistry competition for secondary school students worldwide. Each country sends up to 4 students. Two rounds: a theoretical exam and a practical (laboratory) exam. Tests advanced chemistry knowledge well beyond the standard school curriculum.

name: International Physics Olympiad (IPhO)
description: Annual physics competition for pre-university students from around the world. Each country sends up to 5 students. Two exams: theoretical and experimental. Tests physics knowledge and problem-solving ability at a university-entrance level and beyond.

name: World Scholars Cup
description: A global academic competition and intellectual community for secondary students. Tournaments are held in multiple cities worldwide with a Global Round and a Tournament of Champions at Yale. Covers six subject areas: collaborative writing, scholar's challenge, scholar's bowl, and more.

name: Hult Prize
description: The world's largest student competition for social entrepreneurship. Challenges university and secondary school students to solve a pressing global challenge through a scalable and sustainable social enterprise. On-campus rounds feed into regional finals and a global summit with significant prize money.
